sentences.text: Acanthorhachis was an extinct cartilaginous fish, a member of the class Chondrichthyes, that lived during the Carboniferous period.
Its name derives from Greek words for "spine" and "backbone," reflecting its body, which was covered in spine-like dermal denticles and smaller subsidiary spines.
The type species was originally named Listracanthus spinatus by Herbert Bolton in 1896.
The animal belongs to the family Listracanthidae and is currently monotypic, containing only the single species A. spinatus.
This genus lived between 318.7 and 316.9 million years ago during the Bashkirian stage, with fossils occurring rarely in the Viséan-aged Eyam Limestone of Derbyshire, England.
